source.title: Hunyuan-Large: An Open-Source MoE Model with 52 Billion Activated Parameters by Tencent

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. There are minor extraction artifacts, including page breaks and local file paths, but the relevant scaling-law results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper applies an isoFLOP-style sweep to estimate compute-optimal parameter and token allocations, the same kind of measurement used for compute-optimal scaling, on a new setting: MoE models.
record.gate_note: The paper reports two fitted compute-optimal allocation relationships for MoE models. Benchmark comparisons elsewhere in the paper do not measure pretraining loss scaling or downstream predictability from smaller runs, so they are not included as rows. Cited results from earlier scaling-law papers are not rows.
record.test_reason: The paper runs its own isoFLOP sweep on MoE language models (10M–1B activated parameters, 10B–100B tokens) and fits compute-optimal activated parameters and tokens as powers of minimum compute. That bears directly on V3 in a new setting: sparse MoE with activated-parameter compute accounting.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The paper's overall conclusion concerns Hunyuan-Large's benchmark performance. The scaling section concludes that MoE isoFLOP fits (α=0.5305, β=0.50) imply optima of about 58.1B activated parameters and 5.6T tokens. The authors chose 52B and about 7T, citing the flatness of the isoFLOP curve near the optimum.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an isoFLOP-style sweep, but for MoE models and with a compute formula based on activated parameters plus an adjustment for critical batch size. The authors fit allocation relationships against minimum compute budget.
record.problems: The text gives fitted exponents and estimated optima but no uncertainty or fit-quality statistics. The referenced figures are not visible in the supplied text, so the recorded results rely on the accompanying textual description.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported scaling-law results were left out.

untested.parts: No loss-versus-N/D/C power-law curves are reported.
Optima are extrapolated from ≤1B to 52B activated parameters, but the large run's loss is not compared with any prediction.
Dense models, uncertainty on the exponents, and stability of the exponents across compute ranges are not tested.
No other modality or training regime is tested.
Benchmark scores are not related to scale or to loss.
A non-standard compute formula (C≈9.59ND+2.3e8D) and a critical-batch Cmin adjustment are used, but the effect of these choices on the exponents is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: T3 rather than T1: the method is Hoffmann-style isoFLOP, but the setting (MoE, activated parameters, a modified compute formula, critical-batch adjustment) is new. The Figures 3–4 data are not in the extracted text, so the fit quality and compute range cannot be checked. This is a technical report (preprint), and the scaling fits serve design choices.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute is reported.
No prediction of larger-run loss from power laws fitted on smaller runs is reported.

Tests fitted allocation relationships in MoE models, not dense models or other training setups; it does not report uncertainty on the fitted exponents or a direct test of whether the two exponents differ.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count is reported.
No other modality, repeated-data, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling-law test is reported.
Benchmark comparisons are reported, but not a test of whether downstream performance improves predictably with scale or pretraining loss.
The paper reports its own fitted exponents but does not test whether exponents or allocations vary with fitting choices, setup, or curve bending.

rows.subject: MoE models (series spanning 10M to 1B activation parameters)
rows.operation_detail: Trained MoE models and used an isoFLOP curve to fit compute-optimal activated parameter count against minimum compute budget.

conditions.value: 100B for the model series; data sizes from 10B to 100B tokens were explored
Cmin, adjusted for actual training token batch size using Bcrit(L)

rows.measure: Fitted compute-optimal activated parameter count as a function of minimum compute budget
rows.value: Nopt = Nc Cmin^α; Nc = 5.9 × 10−3 and α = 0.5305; estimated optimal activated parameters approximately 58.1B; the authors selected 52B.
rows.note: The paper says the relationship was obtained by fitting the optimal activated parameter count across minimum compute budgets. The series and fitted result are reported in aggregate.
rows.check: Link and state are correct. The 58.1B optimum is an extrapolation far beyond the 1B-activated sweep and is not checked against a loss measurement. The 52B choice is a design decision, not a result. The fit range in compute is not stated in the text.

source_check.locator_found: Section 2.3.1, Figure 3 caption and accompanying text: lines 334–378.

rows.subject: MoE models (series spanning 10M to 1B activation parameters)
rows.operation_detail: Used isoFLOP exploration and fitted compute-optimal training data volume against minimum compute budget.

conditions.value: 100B for the model series; data sizes from 10B to 100B tokens were explored
Cmin, adjusted for actual training token batch size using Bcrit(L)

rows.measure: Fitted compute-optimal training-token count as a function of minimum compute budget
rows.value: Dopt = Dc Cmin^β; Dc = 3.2 and β = 0.50; estimated optimal training tokens approximately 5.6T; the authors selected approximately 7T.
rows.note: The paper reports the fitted relationship and its estimated optimum in aggregate.
rows.check: Link and state are correct. The 5.6T optimum is extrapolated, and the 7T choice is a design decision, not a result. No uncertainty is reported. Fig. 4 is not readable in the text.

relationships.condition: MoE LMs, activated-parameter compute, Cmin-adjusted isoFLOP sweep up to 1B activated params
relationships.reason: Compute-optimal activated params and tokens both fit powers of Cmin, with exponents 0.5305 and 0.50. This is near-equal growth, matching the Hoffmann form (R1, R2). No uncertainty is reported.
relationships.display_finding: Optimal activated parameters and tokens followed powers of adjusted compute with exponents 0.5305 and 0.50, respectively, without reported uncertainty.
